text:
The points $A(-2,\,5)$ and $B(4,\,-7)$ lie on the line $L_1$.

(a) Find the gradient of $L_1$. [2]

(b) Find the equation of $L_1$, giving your answer in the form $y=mx+c$. [2]

The line $L_2$ is perpendicular to $L_1$ and passes through the point $(6,\,1)$.

(c) Find the equation of $L_2$, giving your answer in the form $ax+by+d=0$, where $a,\,b,\,d\in\mathbb{Z}$. [3]
ms:
**(a)** $m=\dfrac{-7-5}{4-(-2)}$ (M1)

$m=-2$ A1

**(b)** $y-5=-2(x+2)$ or $5=-2(-2)+c$ (M1)

$y=-2x+1$ A1

Note: FT from their gradient in (a).

**(c)** perpendicular gradient $=\dfrac{1}{2}$ (A1)

$y-1=\dfrac{1}{2}(x-6)$ (M1)

$x-2y-4=0$ A1

Note: accept any integer multiple, e.g. $-x+2y+4=0$. FT from their gradient in (a).

**[7 marks]**

text:
A taxi company charges a fixed booking fee plus a constant amount per kilometre. The cost, $C$ dollars, of a journey of $d$ km is modelled by $C=md+c$.

A journey of $8$ km costs $21.40$ dollars and a journey of $15$ km costs $35.75$ dollars.

(a) Find the value of $m$ and interpret its meaning in this context. [3]

(b) Find the value of $c$. [2]

(c) Alicia pays $50.10$ dollars for a journey. Find the length of her journey. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $m=\dfrac{35.75-21.40}{15-8}$ (M1)

$m=2.05$ A1

the cost per kilometre is $2.05$ dollars (each extra km costs $2.05$ dollars) R1

**(b)** $21.40=2.05(8)+c$ (M1)

$c=5$ (dollars) A1

Note: FT from their $m$.

**(c)** $50.10=2.05d+5$ (M1)

$d=22$ (km) A1

**[7 marks]**

text:
The line $L_1$ passes through the points $(1,\,k)$ and $(k,\,7)$, where $k\neq1$. The line $L_1$ is parallel to the line with equation $2x-y+5=0$.

(a) Find the value of $k$. [3]

(b) Find the equation of $L_1$ in the form $y=mx+c$. [2]

The line $L_2$ has equation $x+3y=17$. The lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ intersect at the point $R$.

(c) Find the coordinates of $R$. [3]
ms:
**(a)** gradient of $2x-y+5=0$ is $2$ (A1)

$\dfrac{7-k}{k-1}=2$ M1

$7-k=2k-2\Rightarrow k=3$ A1

**(b)** $y-3=2(x-1)$ (M1)

$y=2x+1$ A1

Note: FT from their $k$.

**(c)** attempt to solve simultaneously, e.g. $x+3(2x+1)=17$ M1

$x=2$ (A1)

$R(2,\,5)$ A1

**[8 marks]**

text:
The diagram shows the triangle with vertices $A(-1,\,2)$, $B(7,\,6)$ and $C(9,\,2)$.

![diagram](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.1_4.svg)

(a) Find the gradient of $AB$. [2]

(b) Show that angle $\text{A}\hat{\text{B}}\text{C}$ is a right angle. [2]

(c) Find the area of triangle $ABC$. [3]

The point $D$ is such that $ABCD$ is a rectangle.

(d) Find the coordinates of $D$. [2]

(e) (i) Find the equation of the line $BD$.

(ii) Find the coordinates of the point where the diagonals of the rectangle intersect. [3]

(f) The line $BD$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $E$. Find the $x$-coordinate of $E$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $m_{AB}=\dfrac{6-2}{7-(-1)}$ (M1)

$=\dfrac{1}{2}$ A1

**(b)** $m_{BC}=\dfrac{2-6}{9-7}=-2$ A1

$m_{AB}\times m_{BC}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times(-2)=-1$, so $AB\perp BC$ R1AG

**(c)** $AB=\sqrt{8^2+4^2}=\sqrt{80}\ (=4\sqrt5)$, $BC=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=\sqrt{20}\ (=2\sqrt5)$ (A1)(A1)

area $=\dfrac{1}{2}\times4\sqrt5\times2\sqrt5=20$ A1

Note: accept the method $\frac{1}{2}\times AC\times$ height $=\frac{1}{2}\times10\times4=20$.

**(d)** $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$ or $D=A+C-B$ (M1)

$D(1,\,-2)$ A1

**(e)(i)** $m_{BD}=\dfrac{6-(-2)}{7-1}=\dfrac{4}{3}$ (A1)

$y-6=\dfrac{4}{3}(x-7)$ (or $y=\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{10}{3}$, or $4x-3y=10$) A1

**(ii)** diagonals bisect each other: midpoint of $AC$ is $(4,\,2)$ A1

Note: FT from their $D$ in (d).

**(f)** $0=\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{10}{3}$ (M1)

$x=\dfrac{5}{2}\ (=2.5)$ A1

tname: Concept of a function, domain, range and graph
text:
A ball is thrown upwards from a balcony. Its height above the ground, $h$ metres, $t$ seconds after it is thrown is modelled by

$$h(t)=1.5+14t-4.9t^2,\quad 0\leq t\leq k,$$

where the ball hits the ground when $t=k$.

(a) Find the value of $k$. [2]

(b) Find the range of $h$. [3]

(c) Explain why the domain of $h$ in this context is restricted to $0\leq t\leq k$. [1]
ms:
**(a)** attempt to solve $1.5+14t-4.9t^2=0$ (e.g. graph or GDC) (M1)

$k=2.96\ (2.96054\ldots)$ A1

Note: award (M1)A0 if the negative root $-0.103$ is also given as $k$.

**(b)** maximum at $t=1.43\ (1.42857\ldots)$ (M1)

maximum height $11.5$ m (A1)

$0\leq h\leq11.5$ A1

**(c)** the model only applies from when the ball is thrown until it hits the ground (for $t>k$ the model gives negative heights; for $t<0$ the ball has not been thrown) R1

tname: Concept of a function, domain, range and graph
text:
The graph of $y=f(x)$, for $-4\leq x\leq6$, consists of three line segments joining the points $(-4,\,3)$, $(-1,\,-3)$, $(2,\,3)$ and $(6,\,1)$, as shown.

![diagram](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.2_3.svg)

(b) Write down the range of $f$. [2]

(c) Find all the values of $x$ for which $f(x)=1$. [3]

(d) Write down the number of solutions of $f(x)=k$ for $1<k<3$. [1]
ms:
**(a)** $f(2)=3$ A1

**(b)** $-3\leq y\leq3$ A1A1

Note: award A1 for correct end points, A1 for correct inequalities (inclusive).

**(c)** attempt to find equation of at least one segment, e.g. $y=-2x-5$ for $-4\leq x\leq-1$, $y=2x-1$ for $-1\leq x\leq2$ (M1)

$x=-3$, $x=1$, $x=6$ A1A1

Note: award A1 for two correct values, A1 for the third (and no extra values).

**(d)** $3$ A1

tname: Concept of a function, domain, range and graph
text:
A farmer uses $60$ m of fencing to make three sides of a rectangular pen. A long straight wall forms the fourth side. The two sides perpendicular to the wall each have length $x$ m.

(a) Show that the area of the pen, $A\ \text{m}^2$, is given by $A(x)=60x-2x^2$. [2]

(b) State the domain of $A$ in this context. [2]

(c) Find the maximum area of the pen and hence write down the range of $A$. [3]

(d) Find the values of $x$ for which the area of the pen is $300\ \text{m}^2$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** side parallel to the wall has length $60-2x$ A1

$A=x(60-2x)$ M1

$=60x-2x^2$ AG

**(b)** $0<x<30$ A1A1

Note: award A1 for $0$ and $30$, A1 for strict inequalities. Accept $0\leq x\leq30$ for A1A0.

**(c)** vertex at $x=15$ (e.g. $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ or GDC) (M1)

maximum area $450\ \text{m}^2$ A1

$0<A\leq450$ A1

Note: FT from their domain in (b).

**(d)** $60x-2x^2=300$ (M1)

$x=6.34\ (6.33974\ldots)$ or $x=23.7\ (23.6602\ldots)$ A1

A1 for local minimum at $(1,\,-4)$

A1 for local maximum at $(4,\,2)$ with correct increasing/decreasing shape

Note: A1 for end values, A1 for inclusive inequalities.

text:
Consider the functions $f(x)=2^x$ and $g(x)=x^2$.

(a) Sketch the graphs of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ on the same axes for $-2\leq x\leq5$. [3]

text:
Let $f(x)=2x^3-9x^2+12x-3$, for $0\leq x\leq3$.

(a) Write down the $y$-intercept of the graph of $f$. [1]

text:
The diagram shows part of the graph of the cubic function $y=f(x)$. The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-2$, $x=1$ and $x=4$, and crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,\,4)$.

ms:
**(a)** use of GDC (M1)

$(1,\,3)$ A1

**(b)** $y=0$ A1

**(c)** local minimum at $(-1,\,-3)$ (by symmetry or GDC) (A1)

$-3\leq f(x)\leq3$ A1

text:
A section of a roller-coaster track is modelled by

$$h(x)=-0.001x^3+0.09x^2-2.4x+30,\quad 0\leq x\leq55,$$

where $h$ is the height of the track above the ground and $x$ is the horizontal distance from the start of the section, both in metres.

(a) Write down the height of the track at the start of the section. [1]

(b) Find the coordinates of the local minimum point and the local maximum point of the graph of $h$. [4]

(c) Find the minimum height of the track for this section. Justify your answer. [2]

(d) Find the value of $x$ for which the track is $20$ m above the ground. [3]

(e) Sketch the graph of $h$ for $0\leq x\leq55$, showing the end points and turning points. [3]

Safety rules require extra supports wherever the track is less than $12$ m above the ground.

(f) Find the total horizontal distance for which extra supports are required. [3]
ms:
**(a)** $30$ m A1

**(b)** use of GDC (M1)

local minimum $(20,\,10)$ A1A1

local maximum $(40,\,14)$ A1

**(c)** $h(55)=3.875$, which is less than the local minimum value $10$ M1

minimum height $3.88$ m (3.875) A1

Note: award M0A0 for $10$ m.

**(d)** $h(x)=20$ (M1)

$x=5.08\ (5.07966\ldots)$ A1

only one solution since the local maximum ($14$) is less than $20$ R1

**(e)**

![expected sketch](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.4_4.svg)

A1 for shape (decreasing, minimum, maximum, decreasing)

A1 for turning points in approximately correct positions

**(f)** $h(x)=12$ at $x=12.68\ldots$, $30$, $47.32\ldots$ (M1)A1

$h<12$ for $12.68<x<30$ and $47.32<x\leq55$

text:
Let $f(x)=3x-5$ and $g(x)=x^2+1$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Find $(g\circ f)(2)$. [2]

(b) Find $f^{-1}(x)$. [2]

(c) Find $(f\circ g)(x)$, giving your answer in the form $ax^2+b$. [2]

Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}$, for $x\neq3$.

(a) Find $f^{-1}(x)$. [3]

(b) Write down the domain of $f^{-1}$. [1]

(c) Find $f(4)$ and hence write down the value of $f^{-1}(9)$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** interchanging $x$ and $y$ (may be seen at any stage): $x=\dfrac{2y+1}{y-3}$ M1

$xy-3x=2y+1\Rightarrow y(x-2)=3x+1$ (A1)

$f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-2}$ A1

**(b)** $x\neq2$ (accept $x\in\mathbb{R},\ x\neq2$) A1

**(c)** $f(4)=9$ A1

$f^{-1}(9)=4$ A1

Note: accept substitution into their $f^{-1}$ for the second A1 if it gives $4$.

text:
A shop offers two reductions on the price, $x$ dollars, of a jacket:

- a discount of $15\%$, represented by $f(x)=0.85x$

- a voucher worth $12$ dollars, represented by $g(x)=x-12$.

(a) Find expressions for $(f\circ g)(x)$ and $(g\circ f)(x)$. [3]

(b) A jacket has an original price of $80$ dollars. Determine which order of applying the reductions gives the lower final price, and by how much. [2]

(c) Leon pays $98.50$ dollars for a jacket after the discount is applied first and then the voucher. Find the original price of the jacket. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $(f\circ g)(x)=0.85(x-12)\ (=0.85x-10.2)$ A1

$(g\circ f)(x)=0.85x-12$ (M1)A1

**(b)** $(f\circ g)(80)=57.80$ and $(g\circ f)(80)=56.00$ (M1)

discount first then voucher ($g\circ f$) is lower, by $1.80$ dollars A1

**(c)** $0.85x-12=98.50$ (M1)

$x=130$ dollars A1

text:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x+4}$, for $x\geq-4$, and $g(x)=x^2-2$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Find $(f\circ g)(x)$. [2]

(b) Solve $(g\circ f)(x)=7$. [2]

(c) Find $f^{-1}(x)$, stating its domain. [3]
ms:
**(a)** $\sqrt{(x^2-2)+4}$ (M1)

$=\sqrt{x^2+2}$ A1

**(b)** $(\sqrt{x+4})^2-2=x+2$ (M1)

$x+2=7\Rightarrow x=5$ A1

**(c)** $x=\sqrt{y+4}\Rightarrow y=x^2-4$ (M1)

$f^{-1}(x)=x^2-4$ A1

$x\geq0$ A1

Note: the domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$.

text:
Let $f(x)=2^x-3$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$. The diagram shows the graph of $y=f(x)$, its horizontal asymptote, and the line $y=x$.

![diagram](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.5_5.svg)

(a) Find $f^{-1}(x)$. [2]

(b) Write down the domain and range of $f^{-1}$. [2]

(c) Describe how the graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ is related to the graph of $y=f(x)$, and hence write down the equation of the vertical asymptote and the coordinates of the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$. [3]

(d) Solve the equation $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $x=2^y-3\Rightarrow2^y=x+3$ (M1)

$f^{-1}(x)=\log_2(x+3)$ A1

Note: accept $\dfrac{\ln(x+3)}{\ln2}$.

**(b)** domain $x>-3$, range $y\in\mathbb{R}$ A1A1

**(c)** reflection in the line $y=x$ A1

vertical asymptote $x=-3$ A1

$x$-intercept $(-2,\,0)$ A1

Note: $f$ has $y$-intercept $(0,\,-2)$, which reflects to $(-2,\,0)$.

**(d)** solutions lie on $y=x$: $2^x-3=x$ (or graph both functions) (M1)

$x=-2.86,\ x=2.44$ A1

![expected sketch](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.5_5-2.svg)

text:
Let $f(x)=x^2-6x+11$, for $x\geq3$.

(a) Express $f(x)$ in the form $(x-h)^2+k$. [2]

(b) Explain why $f$ has an inverse function. [1]

(c) Find $f^{-1}(x)$ and state its domain. [4]

Let $g(x)=2x+1$, for $x\geq1$.

(d) (i) Show that $(f\circ g)(x)=4(x-1)^2+2$.

(ii) Hence solve $(f\circ g)(x)=6$. [5]

(e) Solve $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$. [3]
ms:
**(a)** $(x-3)^2+2$ A1A1

**(b)** $f$ is one-to-one (increasing) for $x\geq3$ (the domain starts at the vertex) R1

**(c)** $x=(y-3)^2+2$ M1

$y-3=\pm\sqrt{x-2}$, reject negative root as $y\geq3$ (A1)

$f^{-1}(x)=3+\sqrt{x-2}$ A1

domain $x\geq2$ A1

**(d)(i)** $(f\circ g)(x)=(2x+1-3)^2+2$ M1

$=(2x-2)^2+2=4(x-1)^2+2$ A1AG

**(ii)** $4(x-1)^2=4\Rightarrow (x-1)^2=1$ M1

$x=0$ or $x=2$ A1

$x=2$ only, since $x=0$ is not in the domain of $g$ ($x\geq1$) R1

**(e)** intersection lies on $y=x$: $x^2-6x+11=x$ M1

$x^2-7x+11=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7\pm\sqrt5}{2}$ A1

$x=\dfrac{7+\sqrt5}{2}$ only (as $\frac{7-\sqrt5}{2}<3$) A1

tname: Solution of quadratic equations and inequalities, the discriminant
text:
(a) Solve the equation $2x^2+5x-3=0$. [3]

(b) Hence solve the inequality $2x^2+5x-3<0$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $(2x-1)(x+3)=0$ (M1)A1

$x=\dfrac{1}{2},\ x=-3$ A1

**(b)** recognizing the region between the roots (parabola opens upward) (M1)

$-3<x<\dfrac{1}{2}$ A1

tname: Solution of quadratic equations and inequalities, the discriminant
text:
A stone is thrown upwards from the top of a wall. Its height, $h$ m, above the ground $t$ seconds after being thrown is modelled by $h=2+18t-5t^2$, $t\geq0$.

(a) Find the time at which the stone hits the ground. [2]

(b) Find the values of $t$ for which the stone is more than $15$ m above the ground. [3]

(c) Hence find the length of time for which the stone is more than $15$ m above the ground. [1]
ms:
**(a)** $2+18t-5t^2=0$ (M1)

$t=3.71$ s ($3.70788\ldots$) A1

Note: A0 if the negative root is also given as an answer.

**(b)** $2+18t-5t^2>15\Rightarrow 5t^2-18t+13<0$ (M1)

roots $t=1,\ t=2.6$ (A1)

$1<t<2.6$ A1

**(c)** $1.6$ s A1

**[6 marks]**

tname: Solution of quadratic equations and inequalities, the discriminant
text:
Consider the equation $3x^2+kx+2k-1=0$, where $k\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Write down an expression for the discriminant of the equation in terms of $k$. [2]

(b) Find the set of values of $k$ for which the equation has no real roots. [4]
ms:
**(a)** $\Delta=k^2-4(3)(2k-1)$ (M1)

$=k^2-24k+12$ A1

**(b)** $k^2-24k+12<0$ M1

roots $k=0.511\ (0.510875\ldots)$ and $k=23.5\ (23.4891\ldots)$ (A1)

$0.511<k<23.5$ A1A1

Note: accept exact $12-2\sqrt{33}<k<12+2\sqrt{33}$. A1 for values, A1 for strict inequalities between the roots.

**[6 marks]**

tname: Solution of quadratic equations and inequalities, the discriminant
text:
Consider the equation $2x^2+kx+k-2=0$, where $k\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Show that the equation has real roots for all values of $k$. [4]

(b) Find the value of $k$ for which the equation has equal roots, and find this root. [3]
ms:
**(a)** $\Delta=k^2-4(2)(k-2)$ M1

$=k^2-8k+16$ A1

$=(k-4)^2$ A1

$(k-4)^2\geq0$ for all $k$, so $\Delta\geq0$ and the roots are real R1AG

**(b)** $k=4$ A1

$2x^2+4x+2=0\Rightarrow 2(x+1)^2=0$ (M1)

$x=-1$ A1

text:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{x-2}+1$, for $x\neq2$.

**(b)** $y$-intercept: $f(0)=-\dfrac{3}{2}+1=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\left(0,\,-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ A1

$x$-intercept: $\dfrac{3}{x-2}=-1$ (M1)

$(-1,\,0)$ A1

**(c)**

tname: The reciprocal function and rational functions
text:
A school is organizing a trip. The cost per student, $C$ dollars, when $n$ students go on the trip is modelled by

$$C(n)=\frac{600}{n}+45,\quad n\in\mathbb{Z}^+.$$

(a) Find the cost per student when $20$ students go on the trip. [1]

(b) Find the minimum number of students needed for the cost per student to be less than $60$ dollars. [3]

(c) Write down the equation of the horizontal asymptote of the graph of $C$ and interpret its meaning in this context. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $75$ dollars A1

**(b)** $\dfrac{600}{n}+45<60$ (M1)

$n>40$ (A1)

$41$ students A1

Note: award A1 for $n=41$ only; $40$ gives exactly $60$ dollars.

**(c)** $C=45$ A1

as the number of students increases the cost per student approaches (but never reaches) $45$ dollars R1

**[6 marks]**

tname: The reciprocal function and rational functions
text:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{3x-1}{x-1}$, for $x\neq1$.

(a) Show that $f(x)=3+\dfrac{2}{x-1}$. [2]

(b) Hence describe a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of $y=\dfrac{1}{x}$ onto the graph of $y=f(x)$. [3]

(c) Write down the equations of the asymptotes of the graph of $f$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $\dfrac{3x-1}{x-1}=\dfrac{3(x-1)+2}{x-1}$ M1

$=3+\dfrac{2}{x-1}$ A1AG

Note: accept working from the right-hand side to the left-hand side.

**(b)** vertical stretch, scale factor $2$ A1

translation $1$ unit right (horizontal translation by $1$) A1

translation $3$ units up A1

Note: accept the translations combined as translation by $\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\end{pmatrix}$. The vertical stretch must come before the vertical translation; the horizontal translation may occur at any stage. Accept a stretch with scale factor $2$ parallel to the $x$-axis in place of the vertical stretch.

**(c)** $x=1$, $y=3$ A1A1

tname: The reciprocal function and rational functions
text:

(d) Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the graphs of $f$ and $g$. [3]

ms:
**(a)** $x=-1$, $y=5$ A1A1

**(b)** $(0.4,\,0)$ and $(0,\,-2)$ A1A1

**(c)** (graph of $g$ also shown for parts (d) and (e))

![expected sketch](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.8_5.svg)

A1 for two branches in correct positions relative to the asymptotes

A1 for asymptotes drawn and labelled

A1 for intercepts

**(d)** $\dfrac{5x-2}{x+1}=0.5x+1$ (or GDC) (M1)

$(1,\,1.5)$ A1

$(6,\,4)$ A1

**(e)** recognizing that the vertical asymptote $x=-1$ is a boundary (M1)

$x<-1$ A1

$1<x<6$ A1

Note: for $x<-1$ the graph of $f$ lies above $y=5$ while $g(x)<0.5$, so $f>g$ there.

The value of a car, $V$ dollars, $t$ years after it was bought is modelled by $V(t)=24\,000(0.85)^t$, $t\geq0$.

A cup of tea is left to cool in a room. Its temperature, $T\ ^\circ\text{C}$, $t$ minutes after it is poured is modelled by

$$T(t)=20+70e^{-kt},\quad t\geq0,$$

where $k$ is a positive constant.

**(b)** $62=20+70e^{-5k}$ (M1)

![expected sketch](qbank/img/gen_math_SL2.9_4.svg)

text:
The population of town A, $t$ years after 1 January 2020, is modelled by $A(t)=12\,000(1.035)^t$. The population of town B is modelled by $B(t)=20\,000(0.98)^t$.

(a) Write down the annual percentage rate of growth of the population of town A. [1]

text: Solve the equation $\log_3x+\log_3(x-6)=3$. [5]

Let $f(x)=x^2$. The graph of $f$ is translated by the vector $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}$ to give the graph of $g$.

The graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is transformed to the graph of $y=g(x)$, where $g(x)=-2\sqrt{x-1}+5$.

text:
Let $f(x)=e^x$. The graph of $f$ is stretched horizontally with scale factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and then translated by the vector $\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ to give the graph of $g$.

Let $f(x)=x^2-4x+7$.

The graph of $f$ is translated by the vector $\begin{pmatrix}p\\0\end{pmatrix}$ and then stretched vertically with scale factor $q$ to give the graph of $g(x)=2x^2+4x+8$.

(a) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$. [5]

The graph of $g$ is reflected in the $x$-axis and then translated by the vector $\begin{pmatrix}0\\r\end{pmatrix}$ to give the graph of $h$. The graph of $h$ passes through the origin.

(b) Find the value of $r$. [2]
ms:
**(a)** $f(x)=(x-2)^2+3$ A1

$g(x)=2x^2+4x+8=2(x+1)^2+6$ A1

after the transformations: $q\big((x-p-2)^2+3\big)$ M1

comparing, $q=2$ A1

$-p-2=1\Rightarrow p=-3$ A1

Note: accept equivalent methods, e.g. comparing vertices $(2,\,3)\to(2+p,\,3q)=(-1,\,6)$.

**(b)** $h(x)=-g(x)+r=-2x^2-4x-8+r$ (M1)

$h(0)=0\Rightarrow r=8$ A1
